html:
The Ndebele kingdom was a military state in what is now south-western Zimbabwe, founded by Mzilikazi and destroyed by the British in 1893 and 1894. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.

Mzilikazi was a commander under Shaka who broke away around 1823 and led his followers onto the high veld, one of the upheavals of the Mfecane. After defeats by Voortrekkers and Zulu armies in 1837, he moved north across the Limpopo and settled among the Shona. His regiments raided neighbouring Shona communities for cattle and captives.

His son Lobengula ruled from Bulawayo from 1870. In 1888 he signed the Rudd Concession, which he thought gave away only mining rights. Cecil Rhodes used it to send the British South Africa Company into the country. The company's forces conquered the kingdom in 1893, and Lobengula died while fleeing. The Ndebele rose again in 1896 but lost, and their land became part of Rhodesia.
